taxonomy.subtopic: Serum potassium redistribution despite total-body potassium depletion

questions.stem_html: A 17-year-old girl with type 1 diabetes mellitus has abdominal pain, deep respirations, glucose of 510 mg/dL, arterial pH of 7.12, and serum potassium of 5.3 mEq/L. The accompanying diagram summarizes potassium movement before and after insulin. Which statement best describes her potassium balance before treatment?

options.text_html: Total-body potassium is increased because acidosis stimulates renal potassium reabsorption
Intracellular potassium is increased because insulin-independent glucose uptake activates Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase
Total-body potassium is depleted by osmotic diuresis even though insulin deficiency and hyperosmolality shift potassium into extracellular fluid
Serum potassium is elevated because aldosterone secretion is completely absent
Urinary potassium loss is minimal because filtered glucose reduces distal sodium delivery

questions.explanation_html: Insulin deficiency reduces cellular potassium uptake, and hyperosmolality draws water and potassium out of cells. Acidemia may contribute to extracellular redistribution. At the same time, glucosuria causes osmotic diuresis, high distal flow, and substantial urinary potassium loss. Serum potassium can therefore be normal or high while total-body potassium is depleted; insulin therapy can rapidly reveal or worsen hypokalemia.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Acidosis does not create a net increase in total-body potassium; urinary losses dominate.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Aldosterone is generally present and may be stimulated by volume depletion.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Insulin deficiency decreases Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase-mediated cellular potassium uptake.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Osmotic diuresis increases urine flow and distal sodium delivery, promoting potassium wasting.

questions.educational_objective: In diabetic ketoacidosis, extracellular potassium may be elevated despite total-body depletion because insulin deficiency and hyperosmolality shift potassium out of cells while osmotic diuresis causes urinary loss.
